summary: First OCCT-vs-truck per-model timing comparison on Falcon-Heavy rows (nozzle_assembly, mvac), facts-gated. Both rows' OCC door runs (door_version 1, fresh process per run) reproduce the recorded OCC reference facts EXACTLY - nozzle_assembly: solid_count 12, volume 50356695.264747284, bbox [[-504.0000001,-504.0000001,-1e-07],[504.0000001,504.0000001,1165.0000001]], 3696-triangle STL; mvac: solid_count 56, volume 0, bbox [[-1462.0,-1462.0,-2730.0],[1462.0,1462.0,2526.0]], 10259-triangle STL - so the OCC side of the facts gate is GREEN and deterministic (conditioning + 5/5 measured runs identical every time), and both rows are fast: ~4.1-4.2 s median fresh door-process wall with door build_seconds ~3.3 s, no boolean ops in either row. The kernel (truck) engine, however, refuses BOTH rows TYPED at the first spline-profile revolve before any geometry fact exists: Refused 'a spline-profile revolve is not a kernel-engine row' with payload {case: unsupported_envelope, envelope: non_canonical_carrier} (door --engine truck exit 1, door_version 2). The cross-engine facts-match gate is therefore RED on both rows: no kernel facts exist, no kernel timing is published, and no kernel-vs-OCC comparison is made (stop condition 1: record DNF-FACTS with the delta, no driver tuning). docs/TT_TIMING_RESULTS.md carries each row's own table - OCC column measured (5 fresh door runs per row, raw samples + medians retained) and the kernel column recorded as DNF-FACTS with the refusal verbatim; no cross-row averages. Finding filed for the funnel programs: the blocker is the same authoring-carrier surface mono's tub hit, one carrier deeper - the truck door regime's lathe arm answers only a closed line-loop profile, while the FH nozzle/chamber/skirt shells are spline-profile revolves over sampled contours (bell_gas_contour/chamber_gas_contour -> bd.Edge.make_spline -> revolved_shell). A kernel timing column on this family requires the truck regime to answer the sampled-contour (spline-profile) revolve, or the recording side to sample it to a line-polyline loop; the FH canonical rows are the natural first rows for that lift.
notes: write_allow was docs/TT_TIMING_RESULTS.md only; the FH tables are appended to that file (the monocoque table from TTC-TIMING-MONO stays intact below the new FH section). Protocol followed per the packet and BENCHMARKS doctrine: cargo build --release --locked and cargo build --release -p truck123d --locked (release regime), timed runs only in a quiet window with no concurrent cargo/rustc/test process on the autobuild farm (confirmed immediately before the measured series), one fresh python process per run, one unmeasured conditioning run per engine per row, five measured runs per engine per row, median reported, raw samples retained, DNF rows kept, no cross-row averages. For these rows the reported wall time is the whole fresh door-process wall per run (spawn to the stdout JSON record): in the truck regime the deterministic kernel executor computes the volume/bbox facts and the STL tessellation inside the door process AFTER the script's build wall, so a build_seconds-only column would hide the kernel's geometry time while including all of OCC's; the door's own build_seconds samples are retained alongside for transparency. The kernel engine refused typed on the gate check for both rows (deterministically, reproduced across conditioning runs), so no kernel measurement runs were made and the OCC/kernel launch-order alternation was moot - the kernel column is the DNF-FACTS record, matching the mono precedent of publishing no kernel timing against a red facts gate. Launch-order bias between the two engines cannot arise because the kernel produced no facts to time. Native module staged per the conformance convention: release truck123d.dll copied as truck123d.pyd beside the interpreter runtimes (python3.dll, python314.dll, vcruntime140.dll, vcruntime140_1.dll, libunwind.dll co-located) and importable from a real 3.14 interpreter.
